section_path: URINARY SYSTEM
DISTINGUISHING NONINVASIVE AND INVASIVE BLADDER CANCER
text: The two main types of bladder cancer are the flat (sessile) variety and the papillary type.

section_path: URINARY SYSTEM
DISTINGUISHING NONINVASIVE AND INVASIVE BLADDER CANCER
text: Only the flat (sessile) variety is called in situ when tumor has not penetrated the basement membrane.

section_path: URINARY SYSTEM
DISTINGUISHING NONINVASIVE AND INVASIVE BLADDER CANCER
text: Papillary tumor that has not penetrated the basement membrane is called noninvasive, and pathologists use many different descriptive terms for noninvasive papillary transitional cell carcinoma.

section_path: URINARY SYSTEM
DISTINGUISHING NONINVASIVE AND INVASIVE BLADDER CANCER
text: Frequently, the pathology report does not contain a definite statement of noninvasion; however, noninvasion can be inferred from the microscopic description.

section_path: URINARY SYSTEM
DISTINGUISHING NONINVASIVE AND INVASIVE BLADDER CANCER
text: Careful attention must be given to the use of the term "confined to mucosa" for bladder.

section_path: URINARY SYSTEM
DISTINGUISHING NONINVASIVE AND INVASIVE BLADDER CANCER
text:
To rule out the possibility of assigning noninvasive tumors in this category, abstractors should determine:
a. If the tumor is confined to the epithelium, then it is noninvasive.
b. If the tumor has penetrated the basement membrane to invade the lamina propria, then it is invasive.

section_path: URINARY SYSTEM
DISTINGUISHING NONINVASIVE AND INVASIVE BLADDER CANCER
text: The terms lamina propria, submucosa, stroma, and subepithelial connective tissue are used interchangeably.

section_path: URINARY SYSTEM
DISTINGUISHING NONINVASIVE AND INVASIVE BLADDER CANCER
text: Only if the distinction cannot be made should the tumor be assigned 1 (localized) for "confined to mucosa."

section_path: URINARY SYSTEM
DISTINGUISHING NONINVASIVE AND INVASIVE BLADDER CANCER
text:
Definite statements of noninvasion for papillary transitional cell carcinomas include

Noninfiltrating
Noninvasive
No evidence of invasion
No extension into lamina propria
No stromal invasion
No extension into underlying supporting tissue
Negative lamina propria & superficial muscle
Negative muscle and (subepithelial) connective tissue
No infiltrative behavior/component

section_path: URINARY SYSTEM
DISTINGUISHING NONINVASIVE AND INVASIVE BLADDER CANCER
text:
Inferred descriptions of noninvasion for papillary transitional cell carcinomas include

No involvement of muscularis propria and no mention of subepithelium/submucosa
No statement of invasion (microscopic description present)
(Underlying) Tissue insufficient to judge depth of invasion
No invasion of bladder wall
No involvement of muscularis propria
Benign deeper tissue
Microscopic description problematic (noninvasion versus superficial invasion)
Frond surfaced by transitional cell
No mural infiltration
No evidence of invasion (no sampled stroma)
Confined to mucosa
